title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
summary: The lens that shows who writes and who reads a ViewModel state accepted only private, internal and protected in front of the property. A state declared with override, the shape of a ViewModel implementing a contract, had no lens at all.

highlights.title: 13 states come back
highlights.description: Measured on a real project of 3558 Kotlin files: 306 declarations were seen, and 13 more appear with the full modifier list.

highlights.title: First tests for the lens
highlights.description: The provider had none. It has nine now, two of which pin its limits rather than its features.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: A state declared with override, open, public or lateinit is recognised like any other.
A declaration quoted inside a string is still not a state, and a constructor call that is not a declaration is not one either.

sections.heading: Notes
bullets: Still out of scope: 24 properties on that project use var model by mutableStateOf. Their writes are plain assignments, so recognising them now would show 0 writes on states that are written all the time.
